cards.text: Moses is still preaching to all Israel, and now he pulls out the calendar. Mark the month of Abib, he says, and celebrate the Passover to the LORD your God. Some people keep a calendar, and I spent YEARS in a junk drawer with no idea what day it was.

cards.question: Why does Moses tie the Passover to the month of Abib?

answers.text: It's when the LORD brought them out of Egypt
It's when the whole harvest is gathered in
It's when Moses first received the law

cards.question: Moses says the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt in broad daylight.

cards.text: The Passover sacrifice comes from the herd or the flock. And Moses is VERY particular about where it happens, friend. Not "eh, wherever."

cards.question: Where does Moses say Israel offers the Passover sacrifice?

answers.text: In the place the LORD will choose
At the foot of Mount Sinai

cards.text: Then the bread rules. No leavened bread with the Passover, and for seven days it's unleavened bread, what Moses calls "the bread of affliction."

cards.question: Israel eats bread that never had time to rise because they left the land of Egypt in ___.
Moses says the unleavened bread is so Israel will do something for the rest of their lives. What?

answers.text: Remember the day they left Egypt
Count the days until the harvest
Honor the leaders who led them

cards.text: And Moses means it: no leaven found in all their land for seven days. That's a deeper clean than my junk drawer got in YEARS.

cards.question: Meat from the Passover sacrifice on the first evening can be saved until the next morning.

cards.text: Moses says it again, plainer this time: not in any of their towns, ONLY at the place the LORD will choose. He's leaving zero room for "my cousin's backyard is close enough."

cards.question: Moses wants the Passover sacrifice timed to match when Israel left Egypt. When do they offer it?

answers.text: In the evening as the sun sets
At sunrise on the first day
At noon on the seventh day

cards.question: On Passover they ___ the sacrifice and eat it, and in the morning they return to their ___.

cards.text: Six days of unleavened bread, and I bet by day five they're dreaming about bread that rises. Then day seven gets its own instructions.

cards.question: What happens on the seventh day of eating unleavened bread?

answers.text: A solemn assembly with no work
A sacrifice offered in every town
A gathering of the first grain

cards.text: On to the next feast. This one starts with a countdown, beginning the day the sickle first hits the standing grain.

cards.question: Starting from the first cut of the grain, how long does Israel count off?

cards.text: When the count is done, it's the Feast of Weeks. Whoever named that one did NOT overthink it, and I respect that.

cards.question: At the Feast of Weeks, Israel brings a freewill offering. How much do they give?

answers.text: As much as the LORD has blessed them
The same amount for every family
A tenth of the very first grain

cards.question: At the Feast of Weeks, Moses tells Israel to ___ before the LORD in the place He will choose.

cards.text: Then Moses reads the guest list: sons and daughters, menservants and maidservants, and the Levite within their gates. The biggest welcome I ever threw was for one scared can opener, so this is IMPRESSIVE.

cards.question: Foreigners, the fatherless and widows are left off the guest list for the Feast of Weeks.
Right after the guest list for the Feast of Weeks, Moses tells Israel to remember something about themselves. What?

cards.text: Feast number three: the Feast of Tabernacles, seven days long. And its timing is tied to the harvest.

cards.question: When does Israel celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles?

answers.text: After gathering from the threshing floor and winepress
Before the first seed goes into the ground
Right at the start of the month of Abib

cards.text: Then that guest list again, foreigner, fatherless and widows included. Seven days of feasting in the place the LORD will choose, and honestly, I'd need a nap by day three.

cards.question: Moses says Israel's joy at the Feast of Tabernacles will be complete. What reason does he give?

answers.text: The LORD will bless their produce and work
Their enemies will leave the land alone
Their debts will all be forgiven that week

cards.text: Moses wraps it up: three times a year, all their men appear before the LORD in the place He will choose, at the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks and the Feast of Tabernacles. Three trips a year, and I get winded hopping across my own bakery on this gold base.

cards.question: At these three feasts, it's fine to appear before the LORD empty-handed.
At the feasts, each person's gift matches how much the LORD has ___ him.

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now. Moses is still preaching, friend, and he's got PLENTY left to say.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 6 quotes "the bread of affliction.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card states that Moses is preaching 'to all Israel.' That comes from outside the passage (Deuteronomy 5:1), but the card cites only Deuteronomy 16:1 and gives no reference for the outside fact.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The question says Israel eats 'bread that never had time to rise.' That phrase points straight to 'haste' and rules out 'silence' and 'shame' before the baker reasons anything out. It also adds a detail Deuteronomy 16:3 doesn't state.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Both blanks test wording the baker hasn't seen and can't reason out. 'Roast' vs 'boil' and 'tents' vs 'wells' or 'fields' are pure guesses, because no earlier card gives context for how the sacrifice is cooked or where they go in the morning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 5 multiple choice, 2 true or false and 2 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop again: 5 multiple choice, 2 true or false and 2 fill in the blank. The type mix is the same as stop 1.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The joke 'Whoever named that one did NOT overthink it' pokes fun at the name of a feast the LORD gives through Moses in Scripture. That points the humor at Scripture or God rather than at Papa Dorin or a human situation.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.

findings.problem: The setup says the timing of the Feast of Tabernacles 'is tied to the harvest.' That rules out the wrong answer 'Before the first seed goes into the ground' before card 10 asks when the feast happens.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The whole passage is rules for feasts and offerings, which the long-stretch section lists as a stretch to sum up in one story card with no choice cards. The passage is also a Sermon (Moses' speech), and the docs say speeches, teaching and key laws are not long stretches. The walkthrough treats every feast rule as a full set of story and choice cards.
findings.question: When an entire Sermon passage is made of feast or offering rules, should it be treated as a speech that gets full story and choice cards, or as a long stretch that gets summed up in one card?

findings.problem: The last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells nothing from Deuteronomy 16:17, yet it cites Deuteronomy 16:17. The citation rule says a story card cites the verses it tells, but the docs don't say what a card that tells no verses should cite.
findings.question: What should the 'verses' field be on a final story card that holds only the 'story isn't over' line? Should it repeat the last verse, use the stop's range, or be empty?
